segments.en: And from the enormity of her pain, seeing that it has been so long and her wound has still not healed, she cries and weeps for a very long time yet remains so distant from Hashem. And therefore "she refuses to be comforted for her children, for they are gone" — as written in the holy Zohar, she says in her heart: "How can I be comforted, when I know that they are gone?" — meaning, "Hashem is not yet with me, for I am so very far from Hashem." Nevertheless, even so — even though she is so very distant — since she still strengthens herself to cry and weep before Hashem always, then Hashem's compassion is aroused and He shines upon her an illumination and strengthening from above, in the aspect of: "Thus says Hashem: Refrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is reward for your labor and there is hope for your end" [Yirmeyahu 31:16]. And all of this comes through the Tzaddik of the generation, great in level, who is the aspect of Yissachar, who shines upon each and every soul and informs it that there is still reward — as Rabbainu of blessed memory taught: there is no despair in the world, for no speech and no cry is ever lost; even a cry from the very depths of Sheol is never lost forever.

segments.he: מֵחֲמַת הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַגָּלוּת שֶׁעִקָּרוֹ גָּלוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁהָעִקָּר עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הָעַצְבוּת הַנַּ"ל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַצָּרוֹת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלָן עַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין לִצְעק בְּכָל יוֹם הַרְבֵּה וְעִקַּר קוֹל הַצְּעָקָה הוּא לִזְכּוֹת לָצֵאת מֵהָעַצְבוּת מִיָּגוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה כַּנַּ"ל שֶׁזֶּהוּ וַיִּצְעֲקוּ וְכוּ'. וַיִּשְׂמְחוּ כִּי יִשְׁתּקוּ וְכוּ' שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמִזְמוֹר הוֹדוּ הַנַּ"ל. כִּי צְרִיכִין לִצְעק הַרְבֵּה כְּדֵי לִזְכּוֹת לְשִׂמְחָה שֶׁהִוא הָעִקָּר... וְעַל כֵּן צְרִיכִין בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְשִׂיחָה וּצְעָקוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְכוּ'. וְהָעִקָּר לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם וּבְכָל עֵת בְּשִׂמְחָה וְכוּ'.
segments.en: There are people who are very, very far from Hashem — utterly so — and who lie in the lowest depths, literally. And when they are aroused and wish to do teshuvah, they have no counsel and no stratagem, and they need only to fulfill the aspect of dam laHashem — blood unto Hashem — and they must cry out from the depths of the heart to Hashem in the aspect of the voice of the shofar mentioned above. And through this aspect, the aspect of dam laHashem which is the aspect of the shofar, they can draw close and return to Hashem even from the furthest distance, for Hashem is full of compassion.

segments.he: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב הַרְבֵּה בִּדְבָרֵינוּ בָּזֶה וְכַמְבאָר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ בְּסִימָן כ"ה בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר מַעֲלַת הַהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְסִיֵּם וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַיּוֹם יִהְיֶה בְּשִׂמְחָה הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ"ל. (הִלְכוֹת הוֹדָאָה הֲלָכָה ו אות כד):
segments.en: Even though they are so distant that they cannot utter any proper word before Hashem, even so they are obligated not to despair themselves in any way, Heaven forbid — only to hope for the salvation of Hashem, in the aspect of "it is good that one should silently hope for the salvation of Hashem" [Eichah 3:26], in the aspect of "he sits alone and is silent, for He has cast it upon him" [Eichah 3:28]. For through silence and stillness one merits to receive from the highest point that illumines into the lowest point — this is the aspect of "for He has cast it upon him." And therefore, through the shofar — which is the aspect of dam laHashem, when one cannot speak at all but can only cry from the depths of the heart — through this the verse is fulfilled: "If I make my bed in the depths, You are there" [Tehillim 139:8] — that one can find Hashem even in the lowest depths, Heaven forbid, and from there all the scattered and lost can draw close to Him.
